description.value: The study investigated fMRI correlates of cognitive control during a Stroop task in individuals with methamphetamine dependence compared with healthy controls, and examined relationships between brain activation, task accuracy, impulsivity, and drug-use history.

spans.text: Then, the Stroop test was presented in the MR scanner to measure brain activation during cognitive control.

design.value: A between-subjects group comparison and within-subjects Stroop-condition comparison were tested using an ANCOVA design with age as a covariate.

spans.text: For that, we set up an ANCOVA design with a between-subjects factor group (MA vs HC), a within-subjects factor task (CC vs. IC), and age as a covariate, and tested for the postulated group differences in the Stroop task.

Impulsivity was assessed by a German version of the impulsive behavior scale, UPPS [ 46 ], exploring four dimensions of impulsivity: lack of premeditation, urgency, sensation seeking, and lack of perseverance.

task_description.value: The manual Stroop test consisted of congruent and incongruent conditions, with participants indicating the color as fast as possible by pressing one of two buttons.

spans.text: All subjects were instructed to indicate as fast as possible the type of color by pressing one of two buttons

stimuli.value: 18 color words were presented in a congruent condition and 18 color words were displayed in one of three incongruent colors.

spans.text: In the CC, 18 color words were presented in the color denoted by the corresponding word; in the IC, 18 color words were displayed in one of three colors, which were not denoted by the word.
